raw_segments.text: A woman who has lost her honor, imaginees that she cannot fall lower, and as for recovering
her former station, it is impossible.
No exertion can wash this stain away.
Losing thus every spur, and having no other means of support, prostitution becomes her
only refuge, and the character is quickly depraved by circumstances over which the poor
wretch has little power, unless she possesses an uncommon portion of sense and loftiness
Necessity never makes prostitution the business of men's lives, though numberless are the
women who are thus rendered systematically vicious.
This, however, arises, in a great degree, from the state of idleness in which women
are educated, who are always taught to look up to man for a maintenance, and to consider
their persons as the proper return for his exertions to support them.
Maritricious airs, and the whole science of wantonness has then a more powerful stimulus
than either appetite or vanity, and this remark gives force to the prevailing opinion that
with chastity all is lost that is respectable in woman.
Her character depends on the observance of one virtue, though the only passion fostered
Nay, the honor of a woman is not made even to depend on her will.
